import hashlib
import json
from cache import make_key
from service import score

# Mock store and compute for testing
def mock_compute():
    return {"result": "computed_value"}

def test_cache_key_consistency():
    # Test key generation for identical inputs
    key1 = make_key("job_text", 1, 1)
    key2 = make_key("job_text", 1, 1)
    assert key1 == key2, "Keys for identical inputs must match"
    
    # Test key changes on any input
    key3 = make_key("job_text", 1, 2)  # criteria_version changed
    key4 = make_key("job_text_2", 1, 1)  # job_text changed
    key5 = make_key("job_text", 2, 1)   # profile_version changed
    assert key1 != key3 and key1 != key4 and key1 != key5, "Keys must differ on input changes"
    
    # Test None handling (implicit via service.py logic)
    store = {}
    result1 = score(store, "job_text", 1, 1, mock_compute)
    result2 = score(store, "job_text", 1, 1, mock_compute)  # Reuse cached result
    assert result1 == result2, "Same inputs must return cached result"
    
    # Test recomputation on any input change
    result3 = score(store, "job_text", 1, 2, mock_compute)  # criteria_version changed
    assert result1 != result3, "Changed input must recompute"
    
    # Test hash uniqueness for different inputs
    hasher = hashlib.sha256()
    hasher.update(key1.encode())
    hash1 = hasher.hexdigest()
    hasher = hashlib.sha256()
    hasher.update(key3.encode())
    hash3 = hasher.hexdigest()
    assert hash1 != hash3, "Keys must produce unique hashes"

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_cache_key_consistency()
